# dbgjs

A command-line JavaScript debugger for **VS Code, Electron, browsers, and
Node.js**. Explore a running application, set source-mapped breakpoints, automate
its UI, and inspect its coverage, CPU profiles, and heap without leaving the
terminal.

```sh
npm install --global @hediet/dbgjs@next
```

The examples below are **recorded from real CLI runs**, not handwritten output.
They use desktop VS Code 1.137.0, a local website, and a running Node
process. Process IDs, URLs, paths, and measurements are from that run, so use
your own when following along. Commands use PowerShell quoting. These are independent
feature examples; the [walkthroughs](#walkthroughs-and-documentation) include
their setup and full execution order.

## Discover and attach to VS Code / Electron

Find windows, renderers, extension hosts, and agent hosts in the process tree.
Select the renderer you want to investigate, rather than guessing a debug port.

````console
$ dbgjs process list --root vscode --no-cmd-line --filter p:33216
VS Code process tree 33216  (6 attachable processes; window metadata available)
└─ p:33216  Code.exe  [vscode-main]
   ├─ w:33216/1  window  readme-demo - Visual Studio Code
   │  ├─ p:10904  extension-host  [extension-host]
   │  ├─ p:22260  file-watcher  [file-watcher]
   │  └─ p:35668  renderer  [renderer]
   ├─ p:12004  cmd.exe  [other]
   │  ├─ p:34684  conhost.exe  [other]
   │  └─ p:37728  wsl.exe  [other]
   ├─ p:19784  Code.exe  [network-service]
   ├─ p:27948  shared-process  [node-utility]
   ├─ p:37388  Code.exe  [gpu]
   └─ p:42028  agent-host  [agent-host]
      ├─ p:5368  Code.exe  [copilot]
      └─ p:36964  whoami.exe  [other]
````

Create a context and attach to the discovered renderer. `--set` selects it for
subsequent commands.

````console
$ dbgjs context create :readme 'VS Code typing' --set
Context readme  rev 1
  Name: VS Code typing
  Connections: none

$ dbgjs process attach 35668 --set
Attachment: created
Target renderer-1  [running]  readme/process-tree-33216  gen 1  rev 3
  Pause: none
````

## Open a website with Playwright or installed Chrome

Use Playwright's bundled browser, or point dbgjs at an installed Chrome
executable. Both expose the same debugger commands.

### Playwright Chromium

````console
$ dbgjs connection add --playwright http://127.0.0.1:54082/ --connection browser --connect --set

````

## Attach to a running Node.js process

Attach to an existing process and inspect its live application state.
You do not have to launch the application through dbgjs. This example's process
was started with Node's Inspector enabled (`--inspect=127.0.0.1:0`).

````console
$ dbgjs process attach 35912 --set
Attachment: created
Target $node-root:process-35912  [running]  readme-node/process-35912  gen 1  rev 3
  Pause: none
````

No second target attachment is needed. The [Express walkthrough](docs/walkthroughs/node.md)
uses HTTP requests to collect coverage and pause inside a request handler.

## Evaluate JavaScript

Evaluate in the selected runtime, or in the current stack frame when paused.

````console
$ dbgjs target eval document.title
readme-demo - Visual Studio Code
````

## Automate keyboard and mouse input with Playwright

Run locator, keyboard, and mouse operations against the **selected page**,
including Electron renderers. Here, real keyboard input opens a new VS Code
editor; the locator waits until it is ready.

````console
$ dbgjs playwright 'await page.locator(".monaco-workbench").click();
await page.keyboard.press("Control+n");
await page.locator(".editor-group-container .monaco-editor").waitFor();
return await page.title();'
"Untitled-1 - readme-demo - Visual Studio Code"
````

## Search authored sources through source maps

Search original TypeScript inside a bundled application without a local source
checkout.

````console
$ dbgjs source grep 'private _doApplyEdits' --path textModel.ts --max-results 1 --context-lines 2
https://main.vscode-cdn.net/sourcemaps/645f29cc3176500b4b5762ba887cf2a7f0ffdf2c/src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts:1503:2
    1501 | 	}
    1502 |
  > 1503 | 	private _doApplyEdits(rawOperations: model.ValidAnnotatedEditOperation[], computeUndoEdits: boolean, reason: TextModelEditSource, resultingSelection: Selection[] | null = null): void | model.IValidEditOperation[] {
    1504 |
    1505 | 		const oldLineCount = this._buffer.getLineCount();

... (3 more lines; full output in the recording)
````

`source grep` limits displayed output to 8192 UTF-8 bytes and individual
source excerpts to 256 bytes by default. Excerpts of minified lines are
centered on the match; line/column and match length remain absolute in
`--json`, alongside `textTruncated`, `excerptStartColumn`,
`contextTruncated`, `outputTruncated`, and `outputOmittedMatches` (independent
of `omittedMatches` from `--max-results`). Use
`source show <path> --line <line>` to inspect the complete source.
`--max-results` separately controls
match count; `--max-output-bytes` and `--max-line-bytes` adjust display
limits. Skipped map/source diagnostics have unknown relevance to a path-filtered
search, so a summary warns about incompleteness; use `--verbose-diagnostics`
and a larger output budget for details. Searches time out after 30 seconds by
default (override with `--timeout-ms`).
Breakpoint failures similarly summarize ordinary nonmatching scripts and bound
human-readable diagnostics. Use `--json` for complete breakpoint assessments
or `source explain <path>` to inspect source candidates.

## Source-mapped breakpoints and live inspection

Set a breakpoint in authored TypeScript. dbgjs resolves it to the generated
script and shows the actual source location.

````console
$ dbgjs breakpoint set edit src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts 1505
Breakpoint edit  src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts:1505:1  [bound; 1 application(s)]
  bound on process-tree-33216/renderer-1: CDP confirmed script 9 v1 at vscode-file://vscode-app/d:/dev/hediet/cdp-client/artifacts/vscode-download/vscode-win32-arm64-archive-1.137.0/645f29cc31/resources/app/out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js:708:1512 via source map MapId(0) (Ordinary)

  Source: ../../../src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts — TextModel._doApplyEdits
      1501 |     }
      1502 |
      1503 |     private _doApplyEdits(rawOperations: model.ValidAnnotatedEditOperation[], computeUndoEdits: boolean, reason: TextModelEditSource, resultingSelection: Selection[] | null = null): void | model.IVali…
      1504 |
    > 1505 |         const oldLineCount = this._buffer.getLineCount();
           |                                   ^^^^^^^
      1506 |         const result = this._buffer.applyEdits(rawOperations, this._options.trimAutoWhitespace, computeUndoEdits);
      1507 |         const newLineCount = this._buffer.getLineCount();
... (2 more lines; full output in the recording)
````

When the edit pauses, evaluate on the live text model:

````console
$ dbgjs target eval 'this.getValue()'
hello from dbgjs
````

The [VS Code walkthrough](docs/walkthroughs/vscode.md) includes triggering the
breakpoint, waiting for the pause, and resuming.

## Precise code coverage

Record function and block execution, then exclude a background capture when
viewing the source-mapped tree. The stored capture stays intact; `--exclude` is
a query option, not a recording option. `HL` means hit lines; `RL` means run lines.

````console
$ dbgjs coverage start
Coverage recording started.

$ dbgjs coverage capture --id background
Captured background.

$ dbgjs target type 'hello from dbgjs'
Typed "hello from dbgjs"

$ dbgjs coverage stop --id typing
Coverage recording stopped. Captured typing.

$ dbgjs coverage show typing --exclude background --path-prefix src/vs/editor/common/model --max-lines 16
Capture typing
185803 RL (run lines), 5427 HL (hit lines)
└─ src/vs/editor/common/model/  [29 files, 5427 HL, 185803 RL]
   ├─ pieceTreeTextBuffer/  [3 files, 1347 HL, 73771 RL]  [3 children pruned]
   ├─ bracketPairsTextModelPart/  [13 files, 1141 HL, 13033 RL]  [3 children pruned]
   ├─ textModel.ts  1091 HL, 56014 RL  [children pruned]
   ├─ intervalTree.ts  863 HL, 18289 RL  [children pruned]
   ├─ tokens/  [5 files, 467 HL, 7210 RL]  [5 children pruned]
   ├─ guidesTextModelPart.ts  273 HL, 317 RL  [children pruned]
   ├─ editStack.ts  155 HL, 1297 RL  [children pruned]
   ├─ prefixSumComputer.ts  56 HL, 15495 RL  [children pruned]
   ├─ utils.ts  23 HL, 115 RL [computeIndentLevel 23 HL, 115 RL]  [children pruned]
   ├─ textModelStringEdit.ts  6 HL, 192 RL [offsetEditFromContentChanges 6 HL, 192 RL]  [children pruned]
   └─ textModelPart.ts  5 HL, 70 RL  [children pruned]
````

## CPU profiling

Record a V8 sampling profile, then inspect the hottest functions with authored
locations. Filter to editor code instead of unrelated runtime activity.
These are real sample measurements, not a fixed ranking.

````console
$ dbgjs profile start --sampling-interval 1ms
CPU profile recording started (1000us sampling interval).

$ dbgjs playwright 'await page.keyboard.type(" profiling the editor".repeat(20));'

$ dbgjs profile stop --id typing-cpu
CPU profile recording stopped. Captured typing-cpu.

$ dbgjs profile show typing-cpu --view functions --sort self --path src/vs/editor --max-lines 8
CPU profile typing-cpu: 4.95s elapsed, 4.95s sampled, 2996 samples
Self       Total      Samples  Function
9.39ms     21.39ms          6  ViewLayerRenderer._finishRenderingInvalidLines  ../../../src/vs/editor/browser/view/viewLayer.ts:536:10
6.28ms     6.28ms           4  _findRegexMatchEnclosingPosition  ../../../src/vs/editor/common/core/wordHelper.ts:164:10
4.54ms     27.78ms          3  ViewEventHandler.handleEvents  ../../../src/vs/editor/common/viewEventHandler.ts:93:9
4.20ms     17.16ms          3  InlineCompletionsSource.fetch → callback  ../../../src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/inlineCompletionsSource.ts:181:20
3.11ms     4.62ms           2  View._scheduleRender  ../../../src/vs/editor/browser/view.ts:523:10
3.11ms     3.11ms           2  ViewOverlayLine.renderLine  ../../../src/vs/editor/browser/view/viewOverlays.ts:163:9
````

## Heap snapshots and instances

Capture the heap and find classes by authored name, even in minified code.
Instance IDs let you inspect objects and follow references within that capture.

````console
$ dbgjs heap capture --id editor
Captured editor (165.4 MiB) in 6.093s: taking 2.530s, retrieving 3.563s.
````

### Run JavaScript on an object found in the heap

Use the instance ID from the snapshot to obtain a live object handle, then run
JavaScript with that object as `this`. Here we call the discovered text buffer's
methods to read the text typed earlier, without needing a global variable that
points to it.

````console
$ dbgjs target cdp HeapProfiler.getObjectByHeapObjectId --params '{"objectId":"3151931","objectGroup":"readme-heap"}'
{
  "result": {
    "type": "object",
    "className": "s",
    "description": "s",
    "objectId": "5915318683987910857.1.167"
  }
}

$ dbgjs target cdp Runtime.callFunctionOn --params '{"objectId":"5915318683987910857.1.167","functionDeclaration":"function () { return { lineCount: this.getLineCount(), firstLine: this.getLineContent(1).slice(0, 17) }; }","returnByValue":true}'
{
  "result": {
    "type": "object",
    "value": {
      "lineCount": 1,
      "firstLine": "hello from dbgjs!"
    }
  }
}
````

These are raw CDP calls through dbgjs. The first `objectId` is the heap instance
ID; the second is the remote handle returned by that call. This requires the
original target to remain connected and the object to still be alive; an
offline snapshot alone cannot execute JavaScript.

````console
Captured 2163x1355 screenshot to \\?\D:\dev\hediet\cdp-client\artifacts\readme\editor.png.
````

## Raw CDP

Use any Chrome DevTools Protocol method through the same managed target session.

````console
$ dbgjs target cdp Runtime.evaluate --params '{"expression":"document.title","returnByValue":true}'
{
  "result": {
    "type": "string",
    "value": "● hello from dbgjs! profiling the editor p • Untitled-1 - readme-demo - Visual Studio Code"
  }
}
````

## Durable contexts and offline evidence

Disconnect without losing the investigation. Named captures remain queryable
after the live runtime has gone.

````console
$ dbgjs connection disconnect --connection process-tree-33216
Context readme  rev 30
  Name: VS Code typing
  Connections:
    process-tree-33216  [disconnected; generation 1]
      Configuration: process tree rooted at PID 33216
      Targets: none

$ dbgjs coverage show typing --exclude background --path-prefix src/vs/editor/common/model --max-lines 8
Capture typing
185803 RL (run lines), 5427 HL (hit lines)
└─ src/vs/editor/common/model/  [29 files, 5427 HL, 185803 RL]  [11 children pruned]
````

## These examples are executable

The README and walkthroughs are rendered from the
[same CLI recording](tests/readme/recording.json). CI replays the flows in
isolated runtimes: stable results must match, while variable measurements must
still supply the promised evidence. No mocks or handwritten terminal output.

```sh
cargo build --locked --bin dbgjs --bin dbgjs-service
npm run generate:readme
npm run test:readme
```

See [generation and replay rules](docs/readme-generation.md).
